sanskrit: taṃ brāhmaṇā vedavido juṣanti; tasyādityo bhām upayujya bhāti sa māsi māsy adhvarakṛd vidhatte; tam adhvare vedavidaḥ paṭhanti
english: The Brāhmaṇas learned in the Veda delight in him, and the sun, drawing its radiance from him, shines forth. Month after month he, the performer of sacrifice, ordains the rite, and those versed in the Veda chant of him at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: sa ekayuk cakram idaṃ trinābhi; saptāśvayuktaṃ vahate vai tridhāmā mahātejāḥ sarvagaḥ sarvasiṃhaḥ; kṛṣṇo lokān dhārayate tathaikaḥ aśnann anaśnaṃś ca tathaiva dhīraḥ; kṛṣṇaṃ sadā pārtha kartāram ehi
english: Yoked to a single steed, he drives this wheel of three naves, drawn by seven horses, he of the three abodes. Of mighty splendor, all-pervading, conqueror of all, Kṛṣṇa alone upholds the worlds. Eating and yet not eating, steadfast as ever—know Kṛṣṇa, O Pārtha, to be forever the Maker; come to him.

sanskrit: sa ekadā kakṣagato mahātmā; tṛpto vibhuḥ khāṇḍave dhūmaketuḥ sa rākṣasān uragāṃś cāvajitya; sarvatragaḥ sarvam agnau juhoti
english: Once that great-souled, all-pervading lord, entering the thicket of the Khāṇḍava as smoke-bannered fire, was sated; vanquishing the Rākṣasas and serpents, he who goes everywhere offered all things into the flame.

sanskrit: sa evāśvaḥ śvetam aśvaṃ prayacchat; sa evāśvān atha sarvāṃś cakāra trivandhuras tasya rathas tricakras; trivṛcchirāś caturasraś ca tasya
english: He himself, as the white horse, bestowed the steed; he himself fashioned all the horses. His chariot has three frames and three wheels, its top is threefold, and its body four-square.

sanskrit: sa vihāyo vyadadhāt pañcanābhiḥ; sa nirmame gāṃ divam antarikṣam evaṃ ramyān asṛjat parvatāṃś ca; hṛṣīkeśo 'mitadīptāgnitejāḥ
english: He fashioned the sky with its five hubs; he formed the earth, the heaven, and the firmament; thus he created the lovely mountains—Hṛṣīkeśa, blazing with the boundless splendor of fire.

sanskrit: sa laṅghayan vai sarito jighāṃsan; sa taṃ vajraṃ praharantaṃ nirāsa sa mahendraḥ stūyate vai mahādhvare; viprair eko ṛksahasraiḥ purāṇaiḥ
english: Leaping over the rivers and seeking to slay, he flung back the very thunderbolt that struck at him. He, as great Indra, is praised at the mighty sacrifice; the Brāhmaṇas alone extol him with thousands of ancient hymns.

sanskrit: durvāsā vai tena nānyena śakyo; gṛhe rājan vāsayituṃ mahaujāḥ tam evāhur ṛṣim ekaṃ purāṇaṃ; sa viśvakṛd vidadhāty ātmabhāvān
english: By none other than him, O king, could the mighty Durvāsas be lodged in one's house; and him alone they call the one ancient sage. The maker of all, he ordains the modes of his own being.

sanskrit: vedāṃś ca yo vedayate 'dhidevo; vidhīṃś ca yaś cāśrayate purāṇān kāme vede laukike yat phalaṃ ca; viṣvaksene sarvam etat pratīhi
english: He, the supreme deity, who reveals the Vedas and who upholds the ancient ordinances—whatever fruit there is in desire, in the Veda, and in worldly life, know all this to reside in Viṣvaksena.

sanskrit: jyotīṃṣi śuklāni ca sarvaloke; trayo lokā lokapālās trayaś ca trayo 'gnayo vyāhṛtayaś ca tisraḥ; sarve devā devakīputra eva
english: The shining lights throughout all the world, the three worlds and the three world-guardians, the three sacred fires and the three sacred utterances—all the gods are none other than the son of Devakī.

sanskrit: saṃvatsaraḥ sa ṛtuḥ so 'rdhamāsaḥ; so 'horātraḥ sa kalā vai sa kāṣṭhāḥ mātrā muhūrtāś ca lavāḥ kṣaṇāś ca; viṣvaksene sarvam etat pratīhi
english: He is the year, the season, the fortnight; he is day and night, the kalā and the kāṣṭhā; the moments, the muhūrtas, the instants and the seconds—know all this to reside in Viṣvaksena.

sanskrit: candrādityau grahanakṣatratārāḥ; sarvāṇi darśāny atha paurṇamāsyaḥ nakṣatrayogā ṛtavaś ca pārtha; viṣvaksenāt sarvam etat prasūtam
english: Moon and sun, the planets, lunar mansions, and stars, all the new-moon and full-moon days, the conjunctions of the constellations and the seasons, O Pārtha—all this is sprung forth from Viṣvaksena.

sanskrit: rudrādityā vasavo 'thāśvinau ca; sādhyā viśve marutāṃ ṣaḍ gaṇāś ca prajāpatir devamātāditiś ca; sarve kṛṣṇād ṛṣayaś caiva sapta
english: The Rudras, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the two Aśvins, the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, and the six hosts of the Maruts, Prajāpati and Aditi the mother of the gods—all these, and the seven seers too, are from Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: vāyur bhūtvā vikṣipate ca viśvam; agnir bhūtvā dahate viśvarūpaḥ āpo bhūtvā majjayate ca sarvaṃ; brahmā bhūtvā sṛjate viśvasaṃghān
english: Becoming the wind, he sweeps through the universe; becoming fire, he of every form consumes it; becoming the waters, he submerges all; becoming Brahmā, he creates the assembled hosts of the world.

sanskrit: vedyaṃ ca yad vedayate ca vedān; vidhiś ca yaś cāśrayate vidheyān dharme ca vede ca bale ca sarvaṃ; carācaraṃ keśavaṃ tvaṃ pratīhi
english: What is to be known and the Vedas that he reveals, the ordinance and the things that it ordains—in dharma, in the Veda, and in might, all that moves and is unmoving—know it all to be Keśava.

sanskrit: jyotirbhūtaḥ paramo 'sau purastāt; prakāśayan prabhayā viśvarūpaḥ apaḥ sṛṣṭvā hy ātmabhūr ātmayoniḥ; purākarot sarvam evātha viśvam
english: That supreme one, become very light, was there before all, illumining with his radiance, he of universal form. Self-born, the source of himself, having created the waters, he of old made this entire universe.

sanskrit: ṛtūn utpātān vividhāny adbhutāni; meghān vidyut sarvam airāvataṃ ca sarvaṃ kṛṣṇāt sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca; viśvākhyātād viṣṇum enaṃ pratīhi
english: The seasons, the portents, the manifold marvels, the clouds, the lightning, and all the rainbow—every moving and unmoving thing—are from Kṛṣṇa; know this Viṣṇu, called the All.

sanskrit: viśvāvāsaṃ nirguṇaṃ vāsudevaṃ; saṃkarṣaṇaṃ jīvabhūtaṃ vadanti tataḥ pradyumnam aniruddhaṃ caturtham; ājñāpayaty ātmayonir mahātmā
english: They call him Vāsudeva, the abode of all, devoid of qualities; Saṃkarṣaṇa, who has become the living soul; then Pradyumna, and fourth Aniruddha—and the great-souled, self-born one commands them all.

sanskrit: sa pañcadhā pañcajanopapannaṃ; saṃcodayan viśvam idaṃ sisṛkṣuḥ tataś cakārāvanimārutau ca; khaṃ jyotir āpaś ca tathaiva pārtha
english: Impelling fivefold this universe peopled with the five kinds of beings, desiring to create, he then made earth and wind, ether, light, and the waters too, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: sa sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caivam etac; caturvidhaṃ lokam imaṃ ca kṛtvā tato bhūmiṃ vyadadhāt pañcabījāṃ; dyauḥ pṛthivyāṃ dhāsyati bhūri vāri tena viśvaṃ kṛtam etad dhi rājan; sa jīvayaty ātmanaivātmayoniḥ
english: Having thus fashioned this world of four kinds, both the unmoving and the moving, he then established the earth with its five seeds, that heaven might pour abundant waters upon her. By him, O king, this universe was made, and he, the source of himself, gives it life by himself alone.

sanskrit: tato devān asurān mānuṣāṃś ca; lokān ṛṣīṃś cātha pitṝn prajāś ca samāsena vividhān prāṇilokān; sarvān sadā bhūtapatiḥ sisṛkṣuḥ
english: Then the lord of beings, ever desiring to create the gods, the Asuras, and men, the worlds, the seers, the ancestors, and the creatures—in short, the manifold worlds of living things, all of them.

sanskrit: śubhāśubhaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca; viṣvaksenāt sarvam etat pratīhi yad vartate yac ca bhaviṣyatīha; sarvam etat keśavaṃ tvaṃ pratīhi
english: The good and the evil, the unmoving and the moving—know all this to be from Viṣvaksena; what exists now and what shall come to be here—know all this to be Keśava.

sanskrit: mṛtyuś caiva prāṇinām antakāle; sākṣāt kṛṣṇaḥ śāśvato dharmavāhaḥ bhūtaṃ ca yac ceha na vidma kiṃ cid; viṣvaksenāt sarvam etat pratīhi
english: And death itself for living beings at their final hour is the eternal Kṛṣṇa made manifest, the bearer of dharma; and whatever being here we do not know at all—know all this to be from Viṣvaksena.

sanskrit: yat praśastaṃ ca lokeṣu puṇyaṃ yac ca śubhāśubham tat sarvaṃ keśavo 'cintyo viparītam ato bhavet
english: Whatever is esteemed in the worlds, and whatever is meritorious, whatever is good and evil—all that is the inconceivable Keśava, and whatever stands opposed to this proceeds from him as well.

sanskrit: etādṛśaḥ keśavo 'yaṃ svayaṃbhūr; nārāyaṇaḥ paramaś cāvyayaś ca madhyaṃ cāsya jagatas tasthuṣaś ca; sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prabhavaś cāpyayaś ca
english: Such is this Keśava, the self-existent, Nārāyaṇa, supreme and imperishable; he is the middle of this world both moving and still, and the origin and the dissolution of all beings.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca brūhi brāhmaṇapūjāyāṃ vyuṣṭiṃ tvaṃ madhusūdana vettā tvam asya cārthasya veda tvāṃ hi pitāmahaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Tell me the fruit of honoring the Brāhmaṇas, O Madhusūdana; you are the knower of this matter, for the grandsire knows you well.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājan dvijānāṃ bharatarṣabha yathātattvena vadato guṇān me kurusattama
english: Vāsudeva said: Listen attentively, O king, bull of the Bharatas, as I tell truly of the virtues of the twice-born, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: pradyumnaḥ paripapraccha brāhmaṇaiḥ parikopitaḥ kiṃ phalaṃ brāhmaṇeṣv asti pūjāyāṃ madhusūdana īśvarasya satas tasya iha caiva paratra ca
english: Pradyumna, vexed by certain Brāhmaṇas, once asked me: What fruit is there, O Madhusūdana, in honoring the Brāhmaṇas, for one who is himself a lord, both here and in the world beyond?

sanskrit: sadā dvijātīn saṃpūjya kiṃ phalaṃ tatra mānada etad brūhi pitaḥ sarvaṃ sumahān saṃśayo 'tra me
english: By ever honoring the twice-born, what is the fruit therein, O giver of honor? Tell me all this, father, for great is my doubt in this matter.

sanskrit: ity uktavacanas tena pradyumnena tadā tv aham pratyabruvaṃ mahārāja yat tac chṛṇu samāhitaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Pradyumna with these words, I then made answer, O great king; hear now, with mind composed, what I said.

sanskrit: vyuṣṭiṃ brāhmaṇapūjāyāṃ raukmiṇeya nibodha me ete hi somarājāna īśvarāḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ
english: Learn from me, O son of Rukmiṇī, the fruit of honoring the Brāhmaṇas; for these are kings among the soma-drinkers, lords over joy and sorrow.

sanskrit: asmiṃl loke raukmiṇeya tathāmuṣmiṃś ca putraka brāhmaṇapramukhaṃ saukhyaṃ na me 'trāsti vicāraṇā
english: In this world, O son of Rukmiṇī, and likewise in the world beyond, my child, all happiness has the Brāhmaṇa at its head—of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇapramukhaṃ vīryam āyuḥ kīrtir yaśo balam lokā lokeśvarāś caiva sarve brāhmaṇapūrvakāḥ
english: Valor has the Brāhmaṇa at its head, and so do long life, renown, glory, and strength; the worlds and the lords of the worlds—all have the Brāhmaṇa first among them.

sanskrit: tat kathaṃ nādriyeyaṃ vai īśvaro 'smīti putraka mā te manyur mahābāho bhavatv atra dvijān prati
english: How then should I fail to honor them, saying, 'I am a lord,' my child? Let no anger arise in you, O mighty-armed one, against the twice-born.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo hi mahad bhūtam asmiṃl loke paratra ca bhasma kuryur jagad idaṃ kruddhāḥ pratyakṣadarśinaḥ
english: For the Brāhmaṇa is a mighty being in this world and the next; in their wrath, those who see directly could reduce this whole world to ashes.

sanskrit: anyān api sṛjeyuś ca lokāṃl lokeśvarāṃs tathā kathaṃ teṣu na varteya samyag jñānāt sutejasaḥ
english: They could create other worlds as well, and lords of the worlds besides; how then, knowing this well, should I not conduct myself rightly toward those of mighty splendor?

sanskrit: avasan madgṛhe tāta brāhmaṇo haripiṅgalaḥ cīravāsā bilvadaṇḍī dīrghaśmaśrunakhādimān dīrghebhyaś ca manuṣyebhyaḥ pramāṇād adhiko bhuvi
english: There dwelt in my house, my son, a Brāhmaṇa tawny as a lion, clad in bark, bearing a bilva staff, with long beard and nails and the rest, taller in stature on earth than even the tallest of men.

sanskrit: sa sma saṃcarate lokān ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ imā gāthā gāyamānaś catvareṣu sabhāsu ca
english: He would roam through the worlds, both the divine and the human, singing these verses in the courtyards and in the assemblies.

sanskrit: durvāsasaṃ vāsayet ko brāhmaṇaṃ satkṛtaṃ gṛhe paribhāṣāṃ ca me śrutvā ko nu dadyāt pratiśrayam yo māṃ kaś cid vāsayeta na sa māṃ kopayed iha
english: 'Who would lodge Durvāsas, the honored Brāhmaṇa, in his house? And who, hearing my reproaches, would yet grant me shelter? Whoever should lodge me—let him not provoke me to anger here.'

sanskrit: taṃ sma nādriyate kaś cit tato 'haṃ tam avāsayam
english: No one would receive him; so it was I who gave him lodging.

sanskrit: sa sma bhuṅkte sahasrāṇāṃ bahūnām annam ekadā ekadā smālpakaṃ bhuṅkte na vaiti ca punar gṛhān
english: At one time he would eat food enough for many thousands; at another he would eat but a little, and would not return again to the house.

sanskrit: akasmāc ca prahasati tathākasmāt praroditi na cāsya vayasā tulyaḥ pṛthivyām abhavat tadā
english: Without cause he would laugh aloud, and without cause he would weep; nor was there then upon the earth any equal to him in years.

sanskrit: so 'smadāvasathaṃ gatvā śayyāś cāstaraṇāni ca kanyāś cālaṃkṛtā dagdhvā tato vyapagataḥ svayam
english: Going into our dwelling, he burned the couches and the coverings and the bedecked maidens, and then departed of his own accord.

sanskrit: atha mām abravīd bhūyaḥ sa muniḥ saṃśitavrataḥ kṛṣṇa pāyasam icchāmi bhoktum ity eva satvaraḥ
english: Then again that sage of stern vows said to me in haste: 'Kṛṣṇa, I wish to eat milk-rice porridge.'

sanskrit: sadaiva tu mayā tasya cittajñena gṛhe janaḥ sarvāṇy evānnapānāni bhakṣyāś coccāvacās tathā bhavantu satkṛtānīti pūrvam eva pracoditaḥ
english: But I, ever reading his mind, had already directed the household: 'Let all manner of food and drink and viands, high and low, be kept ready and well prepared.'

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ jvalamānaṃ vai pāyasaṃ pratyavedayam tad bhuktvaiva tu sa kṣipraṃ tato vacanam abravīt kṣipram aṅgāni limpasva pāyaseneti sa sma ha
english: Then I presented to him the porridge while it was still steaming hot; and having eaten it, he straightway spoke these words: 'Quickly, smear your limbs with this porridge.'

sanskrit: avimṛśyaiva ca tataḥ kṛtavān asmi tat tathā tenocchiṣṭena gātrāṇi śiraś caivābhyamṛkṣayam
english: And without a moment's hesitation I did just so, smearing my limbs and my head with the leavings of his meal.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tadābhyāśe mātaraṃ te śubhānanām tām api smayamānaḥ sa pāyasenābhyalepayat
english: Then he saw nearby your mother of lovely face, and smiling, he smeared her too with the porridge.

sanskrit: muniḥ pāyasadigdhāṅgīṃ rathe tūrṇam ayojayat tam āruhya rathaṃ caiva niryayau sa gṛhān mama
english: Her limbs now anointed with the porridge, the sage swiftly yoked her to a chariot, and mounting that car he drove forth from my house.

sanskrit: agnivarṇo jvalan dhīmān sa dvijo rathadhuryavat pratodenātudad bālāṃ rukmiṇīṃ mama paśyataḥ
english: Fire-colored and blazing, that wise Brāhmaṇa, as though she were a draft-beast yoked to the car, goaded the young Rukmiṇī with his whip before my very eyes.

sanskrit: na ca me stokam apy āsīd duḥkham īrṣyākṛtaṃ tadā tataḥ sa rājamārgeṇa mahatā niryayau bahiḥ
english: Yet not the slightest grief born of jealousy arose in me then; and so he passed out along the great royal highway.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā mahad āścaryaṃ dāśārhā jātamanyavaḥ tatrājalpan mithaḥ ke cit samābhāṣya parasparam
english: Seeing this great marvel, the Dāśārhas were filled with wrath, and some spoke among themselves, conferring with one another there.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā eva jāyeran nānyo varṇaḥ kathaṃ cana ko hy enaṃ ratham āsthāya jīved anyaḥ pumān iha
english: 'Brāhmaṇas alone should be born, and no other caste at all; for what other man here could mount this chariot and yet live?'

sanskrit: āśīviṣaviṣaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tatas tīkṣṇataraṃ viṣam brahmāśīviṣadagdhasya nāsti kaś cic cikitsakaḥ
english: 'Sharp is the venom of the fanged serpent, but sharper still is this venom; for one burned by the serpent-venom of a Brāhmaṇa there is no physician whatsoever.'

sanskrit: tasmin vrajati durdharṣe prāskhalad rukmiṇī pathi tāṃ nāmarṣayata śrīmāṃs tatas tūrṇam acodayat
english: As that unassailable one went on his way, Rukmiṇī stumbled on the path; the glorious sage brooked it not, and at once urged her sharply on.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃkruddho rathāt praskandya sa dvijaḥ padātir utpathenaiva prādhāvad dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ
english: Then, exceedingly enraged, that Brāhmaṇa leapt down from the chariot and ran off on foot by an untrodden path, facing southward.

sanskrit: tam utpathena dhāvantam anvadhāvaṃ dvijottamam tathaiva pāyasādigdhaḥ prasīda bhagavann iti
english: I ran after that best of the twice-born as he sped along the trackless way, still smeared with the porridge, crying, 'Be gracious, O blessed one!'

sanskrit: tato vilokya tejasvī brāhmaṇo mām uvāca ha jitaḥ krodhas tvayā kṛṣṇa prakṛtyaiva mahābhuja
english: Then the resplendent Brāhmaṇa, looking upon me, said: 'You have conquered anger, Kṛṣṇa, by your very nature, O mighty-armed one.'

sanskrit: na te 'parādham iha vai dṛṣṭavān asmi suvrata prīto 'smi tava govinda vṛṇu kāmān yathepsitān prasannasya ca me tāta paśya vyuṣṭir yathāvidhā
english: 'In no respect have I seen a fault in you, O man of good vows; I am pleased with you, Govinda—choose the boons you desire. And see, my son, the due reward of my being well pleased.'

sanskrit: yāvad eva manuṣyāṇām anne bhāvo bhaviṣyati yathaivānne tathā teṣāṃ tvayi bhāvo bhaviṣyati
english: 'As long as men shall feel love toward food, so long shall their love toward you be even as toward food.'

sanskrit: yāvac ca puṇyā lokeṣu tvayi kīrtir bhaviṣyati triṣu lokeṣu tāvac ca vaiśiṣṭyaṃ pratipatsyase supriyaḥ sarvalokasya bhaviṣyasi janārdana
english: 'And as long as holy renown of you shall endure in the worlds, so long shall you hold pre-eminence in the three worlds; you shall be dearly beloved of all the world, O Janārdana.'

sanskrit: yat te bhinnaṃ ca dagdhaṃ ca yac ca kiṃ cid vināśitam sarvaṃ tathaiva draṣṭāsi viśiṣṭaṃ vā janārdana
english: 'Whatever of yours was broken and burned and in any way destroyed, all that you shall behold restored even as before, or finer still, O Janārdana.'

sanskrit: yāvad etat praliptaṃ te gātreṣu madhusūdana ato mṛtyubhayaṃ nāsti yāvadicchā tavācyuta
english: 'As long as this is smeared upon your limbs, O Madhusūdana, there is no fear of death for you, O Acyuta, for as long as you wish.'

sanskrit: na tu pādatale lipte kasmāt te putrakādya vai naitan me priyam ity eva sa māṃ prīto 'bravīt tadā ity ukto 'haṃ śarīraṃ svam apaśyaṃ śrīsamāyutam
english: 'But the soles of your feet you did not anoint—why not, my child, today?' For this did not please me, he said to me, well pleased; and being thus addressed, I beheld my own body endowed with splendor.

sanskrit: rukmiṇīṃ cābravīt prītaḥ sarvastrīṇāṃ varaṃ yaśaḥ kīrtiṃ cānuttamāṃ loke samavāpsyasi śobhane
english: And well pleased he said to Rukmiṇī: 'You shall attain the foremost glory among all women, and renown unsurpassed in the world, O lovely one.'

sanskrit: na tvāṃ jarā vā rogo vā vaivarṇyaṃ cāpi bhāmini sprakṣyanti puṇyagandhā ca kṛṣṇam ārādhayiṣyasi
english: 'Neither age nor disease nor pallor shall touch you, O fair-faced one; fragrant with holiness, you shall do honor to Kṛṣṇa.'

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ vadhūnāṃ keśavasya ha variṣṭhā sahalokyā ca keśavasya bhaviṣyasi
english: 'Of the sixteen thousand wives of Keśava you shall be the highest, and you shall share the same world with Keśava.'

sanskrit: tava mātaram ity uktvā tato māṃ punar abravīt prasthitaḥ sumahātejā durvāsā vahnivaj jvalan
english: Having spoken thus to your mother, Durvāsas of mighty splendor, blazing like fire, then setting forth, said to me once more:

sanskrit: eṣaiva te buddhir astu brāhmaṇān prati keśava ity uktvā sa tadā putra tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: 'Let just this be your disposition toward the Brāhmaṇas, O Keśava.' And so saying, my son, he then and there vanished from sight.

sanskrit: tasminn antarhite cāham upāṃśuvratam ādiśam yat kiṃ cid brāhmaṇo brūyāt sarvaṃ kuryām iti prabho
english: When he had vanished, I laid upon myself a silent vow: that whatever a Brāhmaṇa might bid me, all of it I would do, O lord.

sanskrit: etad vratam ahaṃ kṛtvā mātrā te saha putraka tataḥ paramahṛṣṭātmā prāviśaṃ gṛham eva ca
english: Having undertaken this vow together with your mother, my child, then, with heart exceedingly glad, I entered the house once more.

sanskrit: praviṣṭamātraś ca gṛhe sarvaṃ paśyāmi tan navam yad bhinnaṃ yac ca vai dagdhaṃ tena vipreṇa putraka
english: And the moment I entered the house, I saw it all made new—whatever had been broken and whatever had been burned by that Brāhmaṇa, my child.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ vismayaṃ prāptaḥ sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā navaṃ dṛḍham apūjayaṃ ca manasā raukmiṇeya dvijaṃ tadā
english: Then I was filled with wonder, seeing it all renewed and whole, and in my mind, O son of Rukmiṇī, I rendered homage to that Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: ity ahaṃ raukmiṇeyasya pṛcchato bharatarṣabha māhātmyaṃ dvijamukhyasya sarvam ākhyātavāṃs tadā
english: Thus, O bull of the Bharatas, when the son of Rukmiṇī inquired, I then recounted in full the greatness of that foremost of the twice-born.

sanskrit: tathā tvam api kaunteya brāhmaṇān satataṃ prabho pūjayasva mahābhāgān vāgbhir dānaiś ca nityadā
english: So you too, O son of Kuntī, O lord, ever honor the highly blessed Brāhmaṇas always, with words and with gifts.

sanskrit: evaṃ vyuṣṭim ahaṃ prāpto brāhmaṇānāṃ prasādajām yac ca mām āha bhīṣmo 'yaṃ tat satyaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Thus did I obtain the reward born of the grace of the Brāhmaṇas; and what this Bhīṣma has told you is the truth, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca durvāsasaḥ prasādāt te yat tadā madhusūdana avāptam iha vijñānaṃ tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That knowledge which you then gained, O Madhusūdana, by the grace of Durvāsas—this you ought to expound to me.

sanskrit: mahābhāgyaṃ ca yat tasya nāmāni ca mahātmanaḥ tattvato jñātum icchāmi sarvaṃ matimatāṃ vara
english: And the great glory of that exalted one, and the names of the great-souled god—all this I wish to know truly, O best of the wise.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi namaskṛtvā kapardine yad avāptaṃ mahārāja śreyo yac cārjitaṃ yaśaḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: Come then, I shall tell you—having first made obeisance to the matted-haired god—what good I gained and what renown I won, O great king.

sanskrit: prayataḥ prātar utthāya yad adhīye viśāṃ pate prāñjaliḥ śatarudrīyaṃ tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: Purified, rising at dawn, with hands joined in reverence, I recite the Śatarudrīya, O lord of peoples; hear it now as I declare it.

sanskrit: prajāpatis tat sasṛje tapaso 'nte mahātapāḥ śaṃkaras tv asṛjat tāta prajāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ
english: Prajāpati of great austerity created it at the end of his penance; but it was Śaṃkara, my son, who created the creatures, the unmoving and the moving.
